title: Sabri Guendouz's Hearts role explained and the one-on-one Wouter Vrancken talks
text:
Share

Wouter Vrancken revealed he held a "one-on-one" talk with Sabri Guendouz as the Heart of Midlothian head coach expressed what he wanted from the creative midfielder.

Since joining from Beerschot for a significant six-figure fee in the summer, the Frenchman has largely been a peripheral figure after impressing in pre-season.

He has been an unused substitute in three of the last four Premiership games, as well as across the two-legged Conference League play-off tie with Rapid Vienna.

Vrancken explained the situation with Guendouz and why he has not been used in certain games off the bench.

"I've discussed it with the player, so he knows what to do. Last week, I had a one-on-one discussion with him, or talk with him, not a discussion, but a talk with him, pointing out what I want from him," he said.

"Some games, when he's starting on the bench, some games are not for him to come in in the last 20 minutes. When you need to win every duel, when you have to go in every duel, when you have to show your physicality to defend maybe a one-goal lead, then maybe he's not the perfect profile to do it.

"But we discussed those things, and he knows what to do. I think efficiency and stuff like this is also very important for him.

"He has to, like we said already, adapt to the league and try to improve himself in these moments and take the moments he gets to get better."

Guendouz has been touted as a possible option in the centre of midfield by fans following the injuries to Blair Spittal and Tom Renaud.

Vrancken sees him in a more attacking role, however.

"He can be a lot of things. I don't want to pin one on the other. For me, he's more a 10 and a winger," he said.

"A winger with a free role, I would say. Not a winger like [Josh] McPake, for example, with a totally different style. But he can play from the wing in his role and his style of play."
